KEY CORRECTIONS TO THE PREVIOUS SKELETON (all four review flags confirmed, plus more):
(a) BASE IS NOT A PLAIN Oe108 FLANGE. It is a thin THREE-LOBE plate: three convex lobes at 120 deg out to R54 (R55 = outer envelope/reference), joined by concave R5 scallops. Nothing on the drawing says Oe108; R54/R55 are radii, so the envelope diameter is 108/110 but the profile is lobed, not a disc. The plate is thin (~5 mm), not a thick flange.
(b) MOUNTING HOLES CONFIRMED: 3x Oe10 THRU, on a R50 bolt circle at 120 deg, each inside a 3x Oe20 boss. The previous 'Oe16 lugs' should be Oe20 bosses with Oe10 holes.
(c) CENTRAL TOWER CONFIRMED AS Oe32 / Oe19, NOT Oe25. Stack from the base bottom: body to Z40 (Oe44 est), collar Z40-Z51 (Oe38 est), upper tube Oe32 from Z51 to Z75 (the '25' dim). Bore is Oe19 through the whole part.
(d) CHAMFER: one '2 X 45' callout pointing at the top outer edge of the Oe32 tower. Because the tower is a revolve, the single chamfer shows on both sides of the section, which is why the review inferred '2x 45 deg chamfers'.
(e) NEW - the side boss is INCLINED (~45 deg, est), Oe32 OD with a Oe19 bore, ending in a flat square pad; it is not a plain axial Oe32 boss with a Oe8 cross-bore. The Oe8/Oe6 feature is a SEPARATE small boss higher up on the body.
(f) NEW - 3 radial RIBS (5 mm wide, R2/R1 fillets) run from the central body out to each mounting boss across the lobed plate.

OVERALL HEIGHT: 75 mm (base bottom face Z0 to top of Oe32 tower Z75).

CONFIDENCE: The source is a 474x266 px JPEG screenshot of a SolidWorks session, heavily compressed. All numbers listed under TRANSCRIBED CALLOUTS were read directly and are high confidence. Values marked '(est)' were inferred from geometry proportions, the isometric render, and the feature tree (Boss-Extrude1-7, Fillet1, Cut-Extrude1-5, Plane1, DeleteFace1), because no legible callout exists: base plate thickness (5), lower body OD (44), collar OD (38), collar/lobe-arc centers (50), boss inclination (45 deg), the 25 and 28mm attachment points, and the small boss orientation. The R54 vs R55 assignment is the single most ambiguous read - both leaders terminate on visually coincident arcs; R54 is taken as the solid lobe outline and R55 as the outer envelope.
